findings.detail: Flavour: "Squeeze it before you go down. Tastes like copper and a bad decision." This writes the panel as an activated one-shot heal, which contradicts three stated rules. §2.3 makes grazers the ONLY refill of current Health -- "Grazers refill it... Chase one down, eat it, and you recover a real chunk of current Health" and "Hunting does not heal" -- so no carried object may top you up. §2.1 gives the complete verb list (WASD/stick, lock on right-click/LT, pounce left-click/A, dash Space/RT, poop Q/B); there is no use-item or squeeze input in the game. §2.8 defines panels as what you're "carrying -- what you can do right now, this run, until you swap it", i.e. a standing power, not a consumable. Correction: rewrite as a passive read on toughness with no player action implied -- e.g. "Ripped off something that would not lie down. Bolted on, it keeps you upright a beat longer than you deserve."

All five grazers share the identical idle string "Hunches over the dirt in open ground, oblivious to everything but the ground in front of it, and never strays far.", and it fights their own flavour: Bog Slug "oozes across the mud", Ash Slug "Squats limbless on cooling rock", Tide Grub "chews the shoreline" -- none of which is dirt in open ground. §2.3 fixes the grazer's properties (no colour, never fights, bolts when locked) but not the prose. Correction: keep the rule, vary the habitat wording per biome.

when_locked "Bolts instantly in a straight panicked line the moment it's locked -- no wind-up, no fight, it simply runs and keeps running." is correct against §2.3 ("never fight back, and bolt the instant you lock them") but is pasted verbatim into all five grazers. Correction: same behaviour, five different sentences.

Grazer names double up on two nouns -- "Sod Grub" / "Tide Grub" and "Bog Slug" / "Ash Slug", with only "Scree Maggot" breaking the pattern. Register is right for §3 (primal, crude, comedic); the set just reads thin. Correction: give at least one of the pair a different body-noun.

Flavour "All jaw and gut, built to eat first and think never." is the prey_yellow_* line verbatim, and the same copy-down happens for Red, Blue, Purple and Grey across all 25 Alphas (and the Apex reuses prey_grey_*'s "Meat that's rarer on the ground and meaner in the mouth"). §2.5 makes the Alpha "your equal in rank but fighting at Clash intensity... it hits harder and reads differently than anything you have hunted to get here". Correction: the Alpha should not read as the same animal as the common meat -- give the champion line its own flavour.

Flavour "Watches you from way too far off, then makes you cross the whole gap to regret it." implies the prey punishes the player, while its own when_locked is pure flight ("Skitters backward... before bolting for the nearest hard cover") and §2.2 has smaller creatures flee, "panicking in zig-zags when you lock them". Not blocking -- §3.3 pins Prairies prey at the player's own rank, and §2.2 lets same-size creatures hunt you -- but the line should read as a chase cost, not a threat. Correction: make the regret the walk, not the bite.

Name "Backbiter" plus flavour "Sits in the brush and waits for you to turn around." reads as an ambush predator, while the behaviour block is hide-and-flee only ("Weaves into the nearest cover in tight zig-zags... break sightline"), per §2.2. Same-rank prey may hunt you (§2.2, §3.3), so this is not a contradiction -- but flavour and behaviour should agree. Correction: either let the flavour be about being hard to see, or let the behaviour own the ambush.

Every elite and three of four minibosses carry two different names: "The Meat Wall" / behaviour.name "Knuckle-Slab"; elite_red "The Quickblood" / "The Quickfang"; elite_blue "The Long Shot" / "The Longshot"; elite_purple "The Thicket-Walker" / "The Shiv"; elite_grey "The Iron-Hide" / "The Greyback"; miniboss_claws "Ridge-Back" / "Cragfang"; miniboss_coat "Old Frost-Shag" / "Frostback"; miniboss_heat "Cinderback" / "The Vent-Walker". Only Old Gillmaw agrees with itself. §3.3 has one authored name per creature in creatures.json. Correction: one name per creature.

Panel name "Knuckle-Slab" is the identical string to elite_yellow's behaviour.name "Knuckle-Slab". §2.8 keeps panels legible as a separate register from the creatures that drop them ("The body reads as two registers"). Correction: rename one of the two.

behaviour.name "The Shiv" -- a shiv is a human prison knife, in a world with no people and no tools; §1 states "The fiction *is* the food chain" and §3 sets the register as primal, crude, comedic. Correction: a body-part name ("The Backstick", "The Rib-Splitter") sits better beside the voice reference.

The Alpha naming pattern "The Bloodstreak of the Open Plain" / "The Deadeye of the Broken Crags" / "The Gutslitter of the Ash Pit" uses a grand "X of the Y" title formula that leans a step statelier than §3's primal/crude/comedic brief, and all 25 Alphas share five behaviour blocks verbatim. No invented lore -- no faction, god or prophecy -- so this is preference only. Correction: keep the crude noun, loosen the epithet.

Epithet "of the Salt Flats" for the Beach biome. §2.7 describes Beach as "tidal flats, sea channels and cliffs" with "volcanic vents along the shore"; "Salt Flats" reads as inland desert. Correction: "of the Tideline" or "of the Wrack".

Flavour "Everything you've ever eaten, standing between you and being the only one left." -- §1 states the motivation as "you are trying to sit on top" and to "become the thing everything else avoids", not to be the last creature alive; and the behaviour block is copied verbatim from the Grey Alpha though this is the rank-6 Clash final mirror (§The Ascension). No invented lore, so a nit. Correction: aim the line at sitting on top, and give the Apex its own tell.

Flavour "Soaks the first few hits like a fat kid soaks a dodgeball." -- a schoolyard simile importing humans, schools and sports equipment into a world that has none (§1: "The fiction *is* the food chain -- everything on screen is eating, fleeing, or deciding which"). Crude is on-brief (§3); the reference is off-world. Correction: keep the simile inside the ecosystem ("soaks the first few hits like fat soaks a bite").

Flavour "Chewed through a Rage-tier hamstring and kept sprinting." -- "Rage-tier" is data/UI vocabulary from §2.4b's tier table leaking into authored prose; the fiction should say the word, not the schema. Correction: "Chewed through a Rage hamstring and kept sprinting."

Powers "bite" and "vigour" are not among the four §2.8 names -- "a longer lock range, a stronger dash, a tougher guard, brief camouflage". That list reads illustrative rather than closed, and §3.3 leaves the set to panels.json, so this is not a contradiction; note also that §2.3 makes bar *length* a property of your form, so a "vigour" panel must not read as a longer bar. Correction: confirm the power vocabulary with the Gameplay Engineer against panels.json before ship.

Attach points sit on limbs: "forearm plating" here, "forearm plate" (panel_yellow_bite), "hind haunch" (panel_purple_dash_power), "rear haunch" (panel_grey_dash_power). §2.8 has panels bolt "anywhere across the cube's faces... never crowding the main-face traits" -- correctly kept off the main face everywhere, including the careful "jaw-side flank nub" on panel_blue_bite -- but §2.6a reserves limbs for colour, which mutation rewrites, while panels survive mutation. Correction: prefer torso/flank faces for these four.

Flavour "Rub it on and vanish." implies the player applies it by hand; §2.8 has panels bolt visibly onto the body and grant "brief camouflage" as a carried power. Correction: "Bolt it on and the dark takes you for a moment."

Flavour "Smells like the swamp it died in." is flat next to the rest of the set, and it is the only panel that pins its source to one habitat although elite_blue spawns across biomes (§2.7 palette roll). Correction: give it a second beat and keep the habitat generic.

terrain: "the only biome whose deep end runs Rage from edge to edge". §2.4b puts Rage "wanders the deep ends of Beach and Volcanic", and this document's own beach entry says "Deep and Rage wander freely out here, the full ladder loose on open ground" -- while volcanic's own deep_end says "Deep and Rage wander together out here", undercutting "edge to edge". The qualifier keeps it a claim of degree rather than a false rule, so nit. Correction: drop the exclusivity -- "the deep end where Rage is the rule, not the surprise".

entrance: "gulls-and-crabs country before the vents start smoking" invents off-roster fauna; the world's creature set is grazers, prey, elites, trait minibosses and Alphas (§3.3 creatures.json, §2.3, §2.6). Also the terrain line omits the sea channels and cliffs §2.7 gives Beach, and the Fins+Claws combination it demands. Correction: name the game's own animals, and mention the two traits the ground asks for.

Pocket "A stand of stunted trees in the foothills, below the lethal cold line, where the shaggy grazer-hunter dens among the roots" describes the same fight as miniboss_coat's arena "A windswept shelf in the foothills... matted drifts banked up against the rock". Both correctly place the Coat carrier below the cold its own trait unlocks (§2.6, §3.3 invariant 1) -- they just describe two different places. Correction: reconcile the two arena descriptions.

alpha_lair: "whichever champion you raised, it dens here" -- "raised" suggests the player reared it; §2.5 has "the champion of the colour you ate most" come out hunting you. Also four of five biomes open with the same formula ("still graze soft and Pale") lifted from §2.7's phrasing. Correction: "whichever champion your eating calls out of it", and vary the entrance lines.
